obligation: District notice under the data privacy agreement
citation: District contract and data privacy agreement (contract term); supports the district's control of education records under 34 CFR 99.31(a)(1)(i)(B)
trigger: Discovery of unauthorized access to, or disclosure of, district program students' data (for example, the roster spreadsheets in the "Student files" folder)
notify: District contract contact (phone, then the written notice the agreement requires)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the shortest clock in this matrix; contractual, not statutory

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to the district
citation: Fla. Stat. 501.171(6)(a); definition of third-party agent in 501.171(1)(h)
trigger: Breach of security of a system the company maintains for the district, where district data includes personal information under 501.171(1)(g) (for example, a student's name with information about a mental or physical condition in accommodation notes)
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 10 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe it occurred
notify: The district (as the governmental entity, it then gives the notices under 501.171(3) and (4) for its students)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if the district data is personal information; the 48-hour contract notice comes first

trigger: Unauthorized access of electronic personal information of Florida residents: first name or initial and last name with, for example, information about mental or physical condition or diagnosis by a health care professional (evaluation reports), a government ID number, or financial account data with access codes; or a user name or email address with a password that permits access to an online account. Encrypted data is excluded
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable and without unreasonable delay, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred. A 15-day extension applies only to this notice, if good cause is given in writing to the Department within 30 days
notify: Each affected Florida individual by mail or email at the address on file (for a child, counsel decides how notice reaches the parent or guardian); must include the date or date range, the information involved, and contact details
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company is a covered entity for its private-pay families' data

obligation: Florida no-harm determination (alternative to individual notice)
trigger: After investigation and consultation with law enforcement, the company reasonably determines the breach has not and will not likely result in identity theft or any other financial harm
deadline: Determination in writing, kept at least 5 years; copy to the Department within 30 days after the determination
applies_at_this_tier: Only on counsel's advice; unlikely when evaluation reports were stolen in an extortion attack

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, no later than 30 days after determination of the breach or reason to believe a breach occurred (the 15-day extension does not apply to this notice)
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (synopsis, number affected, services offered, copy of the individual notice, contact person)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if 500 or more (likely if the tutoring platform is breached: about 2,300 current and former students; less likely for the "Student files" folder alone, about 350 students)

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at a single time
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies (timing, distribution, and content of the notices)

obligation: Third-party agent notice to the company (inbound)
trigger: Breach of a system maintained by the tutoring platform vendor, scheduling platform vendor, suite vendor, backup vendor, or MSP
deadline: Agent must notify the company no later than 10 days after its determination; the platform addendum (POAM-007) asks for 72 hours
notify: The company (Center Director); the company then owes the notices above and the district notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - the company still sends the notices

trigger: An affected former student or family now lives outside Florida (online sessions are offered only to Florida addresses, but families move)
notify: Residents and regulators under each state's law
applies_at_this_tier: Check the current address of every affected person

obligation: COPPA Rule: no breach notification duty
deadline: None in the rule. The breach is still evidence the FTC can weigh when judging the 312.8 security program
applies_at_this_tier: No notice duty; keep the incident record for the next risk assessment (312.8(b)(2))

obligation: FERPA record of the unauthorized disclosure (district's duty)
trigger: Personally identifiable information from district education records disclosed without authorization
deadline: The district records the disclosure in each affected student's record. FERPA itself has no breach notification requirement
notify: The district (the company supplies the facts the district needs)
applies_at_this_tier: District's duty; the company supports it under the data privacy agreement

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if a sanctioned party is involved); law enforcement (FBI) or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons; strict liability for payments to sanctioned parties

citation: Voluntary; OFAC advisory (Sept. 21, 2021) treats timely reporting as a mitigating factor
deadline: As soon as practicable (runbook target: within 2 days)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA

deadline: Per policy: prompt notice; call the carrier's breach hotline before hiring vendors

obligation: Title IV breach report to FSA
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach at a Title IV institution or servicer
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach
notify: FSA (CPSSAIG@ed.gov and/or the FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form)
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a Title IV participant and has no SAIG agreement

trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after discovery
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company is not a financial institution under the Safeguards Rule (no Title IV participation and no financing)

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident (reasonable belief) or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after a ransom payment
applies_at_this_tier: No - NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25 (reporting is voluntary until then). The proposed criteria (education agencies with 1,000 or more students, Title IV institutions, or entities above the SBA size standard) would not reach the company

obligation: Covered telecommunications equipment or services discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services
deadline: Within 1 business day of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts

citation: FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies a covered article (Kaspersky Lab hardware, software, or services)
deadline: Within 3 business days of identification (further report within 10 business days). Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
applies_at_this_tier: No - the company holds no federal contracts or subcontracts
